## How it works

- [statement] The Morgana Countron AT Touch page uses different mechanism labels: its descriptive paragraph says twin-blade counting, while its specification field says Pin & blade. Preserve both descriptions pending model-specific clarification. (low confidence) — https://plockmaticgroup.com/morgana/product/countron-touch-at/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] Uchida describes EZC-250 batch counting and interval timing as helping an operator collect a designated number of items; it also describes automatic retry after a slipped feed. Treat operator collection as a labor step when evaluating this counter. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/products/detail/id=287 · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Duplo lists a DSC-10/60i input minimum of 4.1 x 5.8 inches and a maximum rated speed of 10,000 sets per hour. These are document-collator specifications, not demonstrated finished-card deck throughput; smaller finished cards require a different documented feeding solution. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dsc-10-60i-collator/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] Madison advertises card-line counting, stacking and banding for cards starting at 3 x 3 inches. Its SB-25 waits for a predetermined count or an upstream sort signal before banding; the advertised minimum size needs checking against the actual cards. (low confidence) — https://www.madisonbanders.com/applications/card-sorting-gift-cards · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] MBM’s AeroCut X product page rates speed at 24 sheets/minute for two cuts and one crease on an 8 1/2 × 11 sheet. That rating does not measure completed rounded playing-card decks. (low confidence) — https://mbmcorp.com/product/aerocut-x-digital-print-finisher/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Sheet cutting slitting and corner rounding

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Marden Edwards distinguishes LX, LX wide and LXH maximum wrapping rates as 70, 40 and 90 packs per minute, respectively, and explicitly says output depends on pack size. The 90-pack headline cannot be applied to every LX configuration or treated as measured complete-game output. (low confidence) — https://www.mardenedwards.com/machinery/overwrapping-machines/lx-series · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] In a supplier-authored playing-card plant case study, EXAIR reports that cards stuck together and double-fed, and that static regenerated through the process. This is evidence of a real feeding failure mode; it does not establish a universal failure rate or quantified throughput improvement. (low confidence) — https://blog.exair.com/2022/01/19/playing-card-manufacturer-gets-dealt-a-bad-hand-from-static-electricity/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] TCG Machines documents feed-mechanism adjustment, dirty feed wheels, and insufficient card weight as causes of its PhyzBatch Refill Hopper error. This adjacent card-handling example shows why automated feeding still requires setup and maintenance; its intervals must not be transferred to a manufacturing line. (low confidence) — https://support.tcgmachines.com/knowledge/error-empty-hopper · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] The CR-50 manual rates Standard/Special cutting units for paper stacks up to 1/2 inch and Large cutting units for stacks up to 1/8 inch. The applicable stack limit depends on the installed cutting-unit class. (low confidence) — https://www.lasscowizer.com/cmsb/uploads/cr50-manual-small.pdf · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Sheet cutting slitting and corner rounding
- [statement] Print & Finishing Solutions identifies a nicked blade as a possible cause of ragged slit edges. Treat this as dealer troubleshooting guidance, not a measured failure rate. (low confidence) — https://www.pfsgraphics.com/resources-slitter-cutters-trimmers · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Sheet cutting slitting and corner rounding
- [statement] In an April 2024 PrintPlanet thread, operator COGordon reported Duplo 646 double-feeding on stocks lighter than card stock despite service-company settings. This is an anecdote about that machine, not a failure-rate measurement or evidence against the DC-746. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/methods-for-reducing-static-on-duplo-646.294079/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Sheet cutting slitting and corner rounding · also: https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-746-slitter-cutter-creaser/
- [statement] Summa documents a recovery path when the camera cannot recognize printed marks: edit the camera profile or select the current position to identify a poorly printed mark. Automatic registration can require operator intervention. (low confidence) — https://support.summa.eu/support/solutions/articles/43000493939-what-if-goproduce-does-not-recognize-registration-marks- · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Vision inspection and automatic sheet registration
- [statement] For camera automatic-setup failure, the SmartSlitter manual directs attention to illumination angle and optical focus. Allow troubleshooting effort when evaluating short-run setup burden. (low confidence) — https://www.pfsdocs.com/new-equipment/digital-bindery/slitter-cutter-creasers/technical/Horizon_SmartSlitter_OM.pdf · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Vision inspection and automatic sheet registration
- [statement] A DC-646 operator reported reliable optical-mark reading on coated substrates but rejection problems on uncoated substrates. This is one attributed stock-dependent failure report, without a verified cause or a population failure-rate estimate. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/duplo-dc-646-optical-registration-mark-not-reading.294834/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Vision inspection and automatic sheet registration

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Rollem describes an Auto-Collator that combines sub-packs into complete sets and an additional in-line cello-wrap unit; this is evidence of a modular collation-to-wrapping workflow, rather than proof that a collator itself loads retail boxes. (low confidence) — https://www.rollemusa.com/feeding-delivery-units/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation · also: https://rollem.com/processes/collate/
- [statement] Pineberry lists standard CC-50 batch capabilities of 1–100. Its announcement for the 2018 ICMA exhibition additionally says higher counts are available. Treat the higher-count configuration as an unresolved specification. If a proposed stack exceeds the standard batch range, confirm the higher-count configuration rather than assuming the standard counter can process it in one batch. (low confidence) — https://www.pineberryinc.com/solutions/collectible-card-sorting-counting-machines/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation · also: https://www.pineberryinc.com/press-release/pineberry-manufacturing-to-demonstrate-the-cc-50-card-counter-at-icma-expo-2018/
- [statement] Uchida specifies EZC-250 items 0.2–0.8mm thick, 25–120mm wide and 40–150mm long, with a stack capacity up to 130mm. Items must be flat, uncurled and without burrs; nonrectangular shapes require testing. These are stock qualification limits rather than proof of compatibility with the game. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/products/detail/id=287 · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] Uchida describes Countron OP as an optical counter using an optical sensor and air blow. Its standard TD1 sensor covers 0.18–0.35mm material and its specification says no tab tape insertion. Treat it as quantity-verification equipment, rather than an automatic physical separator for finished decks. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/products/detail/id=285 · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] Rollem markets the AutoCollator for lower-volume and short-run card jobs, with collected decks presented to downstream wrapping or packing; these are described as downstream processes rather than functions established by the collator description. (low confidence) — https://rollem.com/processes/collate/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] PrintNinja describes a stack smoothing/rounding operation after trimming, while its domestic rotary-die route forms final size and rounded corners together. These are alternative production routes, rather than a requirement that every card use both. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/card-game-production/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Sheet cutting slitting and corner rounding
- [statement] Canon identifies changes in substrate supply or batch as reasons image alignment may need attention and explicitly lists front-versus-back misalignment. Repeated artwork alone does not establish duplex alignment consistency. (low confidence) — https://docs.cpp.canon/help?pageid=M143919.xml&tsm=ODP000166-8.1EN.US · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Vision inspection and automatic sheet registration

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Collation, card counting, and banding are distinct operations: Rollem describes arranging cards into decks, Pineberry describes counting individual cards, and Madison describes counting, stacking and banding. Specify which operations a proposed line actually includes. (medium confidence) — https://rollem.com/processes/collate/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation · also: https://www.pineberryinc.com/solutions/collectible-card-sorting-counting-machines/, https://www.madisonbanders.com/applications/card-sorting-gift-cards
- [statement] The Morgana Countron AT Touch page specifies an optional small-paper attachment with a minimum size of seventy by one hundred sixty millimeters and tab insertion every 2–1,000 sheets. A sheet-counting specification must therefore be checked against the actual finished-card dimensions before selection. (low confidence) — https://plockmaticgroup.com/morgana/product/countron-touch-at/ · keywords: Playing-card deck cutting collation and packaging automation, Deck collation counting and packing automation
- [statement] The same EXAIR case study describes a card-production line that boxed and labelled its output. It is an attributed example of downstream boxing automation. If a custom game is proposed, verify its required configuration before using the case-study line as a production model. - [statement] Rollem describes SlipStream III collation as collecting rows of cards into sub-decks and sequencing them in a Pack Separation Unit; its software can combine multiple sub-decks so a deck may span multiple sheets or one sheet may produce multiple decks. This is manufacturer-described capability, not verification of the commissioned two-stack game.
